mpt-course-english-d10q10.q: Which sentence expresses an outside obligation rather than the speaker’s own?
o: You must submit the form by Friday.
You have to submit the form by Friday; it is a departmental rule.
You should submit the form by Friday.
You may submit the form by Friday.
mpt-course-english-d10q10.e: Have to points to an external rule; must usually carries the speaker’s own authority.

mpt-course-english-d10q2.q: He ____ the file; he was on leave all week.
mpt-course-english-d10q2.e: Can’t have + participle expresses a confident denial about the past.

mpt-course-english-d10q3.q: Which sentence uses the subjunctive correctly?
o: The court ordered that the record be produced.
The court ordered that the record is produced.
The court ordered that the record producing.
The court ordered that the record produces.
mpt-course-english-d10q3.e: After order, demand or recommend, a that-clause takes the bare form.

mpt-course-english-d10q4.q: You ____ paid the fine; the notice had already been withdrawn.
mpt-course-english-d10q4.e: Need not have + participle means the action was done but was unnecessary.

mpt-course-english-d10q5.q: Find the error: “Candidates will can apply (A) online from Monday (B) until the closing date (C) in March (D).”
mpt-course-english-d10q5.e: Two modals cannot combine. Write “will be able to apply”.

mpt-course-english-d10q6.q: If she had accepted the posting, she ____ in Gilgit now.
mpt-course-english-d10q6.e: A past condition with a present result is a mixed conditional: would + bare infinitive.

o: You must not enter the examination hall with a phone.
You need not enter the examination hall with a phone.
You could not enter the hall with a phone.
You may not want to enter the hall with a phone.
mpt-course-english-d10q7.e: Must not forbids; need not merely removes an obligation.

mpt-course-english-d10q8.q: Find the error: “It is essential that every candidate carries (A) a valid identity card (B) and reports (C) an hour early (D).”
mpt-course-english-d10q8.e: It is essential that takes the subjunctive: carry, and correspondingly report.

mpt-course-english-d10q9.q: ____ the funds been released on time, the project would have finished within budget.
mpt-course-english-d10q9.e: Inverting had replaces if in a formal third conditional.

mpt-course-english-d11q1.q: Find the error: “The draft policy (A) has circulated (B) to all provincial departments (C) for comment (D).”
mpt-course-english-d11q1.e: The draft did not circulate anything: it needs the passive has been circulated.

mpt-course-english-d11q10.q: The accounts ____ externally every year, as the rules require.

mpt-course-english-d11q2.q: Convert to the passive: “The registrar had issued the notice.”
o: The notice was issued by the registrar.
The notice had issued by the registrar.
The notice had been issued by the registrar.
The notice has been issued by the registrar.
mpt-course-english-d11q2.e: Past perfect active becomes had been + participle.

mpt-course-english-d11q3.q: Convert to the passive: “Close the gate at sunset.”
o: The gate was closed at sunset.
The gate is closed at sunset by you.
Let the gate be closed at sunset.
mpt-course-english-d11q3.e: An imperative becomes “Let … be + participle” or “… should be + participle”.

mpt-course-english-d11q4.q: It ____ that the department ignored the earlier warnings.
mpt-course-english-d11q4.e: The impersonal passive of a reporting verb is it is + participle + that.

mpt-course-english-d11q5.q: Find the error: “By whom (A) the decision (B) was taken (C) remains unclear (D).”
mpt-course-english-d11q5.e: The passive question requires inversion: “By whom the decision was taken” works only as an embedded clause; as a direct question it must be “By whom was the decision taken?”

mpt-course-english-d11q6.q: Which sentence uses the causative correctly?
o: I got repaired my car yesterday.
I had repaired my car by the mechanic.
I had my car repaired yesterday.
I was repaired my car yesterday.
mpt-course-english-d11q6.e: have + object + past participle, in that order.

mpt-course-english-d11q7.q: The applicant ____ a notice of hearing last week.
mpt-course-english-d11q7.e: With a two-object verb, the person may become the passive subject: the applicant was sent a notice.

mpt-course-english-d11q9.q: Which version is better in an essay paragraph about your own argument?
o: Reform is argued to be necessary by this writer.
It is argued by this writer that reform is necessary.
Reform is necessary for three reasons.
Reform, it is argued, is necessary.
mpt-course-english-d11q9.e: State the claim directly. Passive self-reference wastes words and weakens the argument.

mpt-course-english-d12q1.q: Report: “Have you seen the notification?” the clerk asked.
o: The clerk asked whether I had seen the notification.
The clerk asked have I seen the notification.
The clerk asked whether had I seen the notification.
The clerk asked that whether I had seen the notification.
mpt-course-english-d12q1.e: Yes-or-no questions take if or whether and statement order.

mpt-course-english-d12q10.q: Which sentence correctly reports “Let us postpone the meeting”?
o: He asked to postpone the meeting that.
He told that they postpone the meeting.
He suggested that the meeting should be postponed.
He said let us postpone the meeting.
mpt-course-english-d12q10.e: Let us is reported with suggest + that-clause or suggest + -ing.

mpt-course-english-d12q3.q: Report: “Do not touch the exhibits,” the guide warned us.
o: The guide warned us that we do not touch the exhibits.
The guide warned us to not touching the exhibits.
The guide warned us not to touch the exhibits.
The guide warned us that do not touch the exhibits.
mpt-course-english-d12q3.e: A negative command becomes not to + infinitive.

mpt-course-english-d12q4.q: She said that she ____ the file the previous day.
mpt-course-english-d12q4.e: A past simple in direct speech backshifts to the past perfect.

mpt-course-english-d12q6.q: Which report keeps the present tense correctly?
o: The teacher said that the sun rose in the east.
The teacher said that the sun rises in the east.
The teacher said that the sun had risen in the east.
The teacher said that the sun would rise in the east.
mpt-course-english-d12q6.e: A permanent truth is not backshifted.

mpt-course-english-d12q7.q: “You must submit it today.” → He said that I ____ submit it that day.
mpt-course-english-d12q7.e: Must backshifts to had to when it expresses obligation.

mpt-course-english-d12q8.q: Report: “Please lend me your notes,” he said to her.
o: He requested her to lend him her notes.
He said her to lend him her notes.
He told her that please lend him her notes.
He requested her that she lends him her notes.
mpt-course-english-d12q8.e: A polite request becomes request/ask + person + to + infinitive.

mpt-course-english-d13q1.q: Find the error: “He is one of (A) the most competent officer (B) in the division (C) this year (D).”
mpt-course-english-d13q1.e: One of the + superlative requires a plural noun: officers.

mpt-course-english-d13q10.q: Only ____ few candidates attempted ____ last question.
mpt-course-english-d13q10.e: A few means some; the last question is identified by the ordinal.

mpt-course-english-d13q2.q: ____ poor in ____ rural areas have little access to credit.
mpt-course-english-d13q2.e: The + adjective names a class of people; rural areas in a general sense takes no article.

mpt-course-english-d13q4.q: The accused was released from ____ prison after ____ appeal succeeded.
mpt-course-english-d13q4.e: In or from prison as an inmate takes no article; the appeal is the specific one mentioned.

mpt-course-english-d13q5.q: Find the error: “The Pakistan (A) is a member (B) of the United Nations (C) and the Commonwealth (D).”
mpt-course-english-d13q5.e: A single-word country name takes no article; organisation names with of or plural forms do.

mpt-course-english-d13q7.q: It was ____ honour to serve on ____ committee that drafted the policy.
mpt-course-english-d13q7.e: Honour has a silent h; the relative clause identifies which committee.

mpt-course-english-d13q8.q: Find the error: “The unemployment (A) among young graduates (B) has risen (C) sharply since 2019 (D).”
mpt-course-english-d13q8.e: Unemployment here is a general abstract noun and takes no article.

mpt-course-english-d14q10.q: Which sentence has a clear reference for This?
o: The department delayed the audit for two years. This is unacceptable.
The department delayed the audit for two years. This delay is unacceptable.
This is why the department delayed the audit.
mpt-course-english-d14q10.e: This + a noun names exactly what is being criticised.

mpt-course-english-d14q4.q: She is the scholar ____ work on land reform is most often cited.
mpt-course-english-d14q4.e: Possession requires whose; who’s means who is.

mpt-course-english-d14q5.q: Which sentence is free of ambiguity?
o: The principal told the teacher that she had been promoted.
The principal informed the teacher of the teacher’s promotion.
She told her that she had been promoted.
The principal told her that she had been promoted.
mpt-course-english-d14q5.e: Only option B makes it certain who was promoted.

mpt-course-english-d14q6.q: Find the error: “Myself and two colleagues (A) prepared the draft (B) over three days (C) in the secretariat (D).”
mpt-course-english-d14q6.e: A reflexive cannot be a subject: “Two colleagues and I prepared …”.

mpt-course-english-d14q7.q: He performed better in the interview than ____.
mpt-course-english-d14q7.e: Complete the comparison: better than I did. The subject form is needed.

mpt-course-english-d14q8.q: Which sentence uses the reflexive correctly?
o: The officers reviewed the file theirselves.
The minister himself reviewed the file.
Please forward the file to myself.
mpt-course-english-d14q8.e: A reflexive may be used for emphasis beside the subject it echoes.

mpt-course-english-d15q1.s: Modifiers: put the describing words where they belong
mpt-course-english-d15q1.q: Find the error: “Driving through the flooded district (A), the damaged bridges (B) were clearly visible (C) from the road (D).”
mpt-course-english-d15q1.e: Bridges do not drive. Name the traveller: “we could clearly see the damaged bridges”.

mpt-course-english-d15q10.s: Modifiers: put the describing words where they belong
mpt-course-english-d15q10.q: Find the error: “He said he would (A) only sign the file (B) after the legal branch (C) had cleared it (D).”
mpt-course-english-d15q10.e: The limit is on the timing, not the act: “he would sign the file only after the legal branch had cleared it”.

mpt-course-english-d15q2.s: Modifiers: put the describing words where they belong
mpt-course-english-d15q2.q: Which sentence places the modifier correctly?
o: The department almost has released all the funds.
Almost the department has released all the funds.
The department has released almost all the funds.
The department has almost released all the funds.
mpt-course-english-d15q2.e: Almost limits the quantity, so it belongs beside all the funds.

mpt-course-english-d15q3.s: Modifiers: put the describing words where they belong
mpt-course-english-d15q3.q: Find the error: “The report criticised the contractor (A) for the delay (B) which ran to (C) four hundred pages (D).”
mpt-course-english-d15q3.e: The relative clause describes the report, not the delay. Move it: “The report, which ran to four hundred pages, criticised …”.

mpt-course-english-d15q4.s: Modifiers: put the describing words where they belong
o: Students who study regularly often succeed.
Students who study succeed often regularly.
mpt-course-english-d15q4.e: In option B, often squints between study and succeed.

mpt-course-english-d15q5.s: Modifiers: put the describing words where they belong
mpt-course-english-d15q5.q: The minister ____ been criticised for the appointment.
mpt-course-english-d15q5.e: A frequency adverb follows the first auxiliary: has repeatedly been criticised.

mpt-course-english-d15q6.s: Modifiers: put the describing words where they belong
mpt-course-english-d15q6.q: Find the error: “To qualify for the scholarship (A), a minimum of sixty per cent marks (B) is required (C) in the last degree (D).”
mpt-course-english-d15q6.e: Marks do not qualify for a scholarship. Write “a candidate must obtain a minimum of sixty per cent”.

mpt-course-english-d15q7.s: Modifiers: put the describing words where they belong
mpt-course-english-d15q7.e: Size precedes age, which precedes material.

mpt-course-english-d15q8.s: Modifiers: put the describing words where they belong
mpt-course-english-d15q8.q: Find the error: “The scheme, after several years of delay and three separate inquiries into its finances (A), was (B) finally (C) abandoned (D).”
mpt-course-english-d15q8.e: The long insertion separates the subject from its verb. Move it: “After several years of delay and three separate inquiries into its finances, the scheme was finally abandoned.”

mpt-course-english-d16q2.q: There is no easy solution ____ the energy crisis.

mpt-course-english-d16q5.q: The new duty had a significant effect ____ import volumes.
mpt-course-english-d16q5.e: Effect on is the fixed partnership; affect is the verb.

mpt-course-english-d16q8.q: He arrived ____ time for the interview but not ____ time to revise his notes.
mpt-course-english-d16q8.e: On time = punctual; in time = early enough for something.

mpt-course-english-d17q1.q: Find the error: “The board suggested (A) to reconsider (B) the eligibility rules (C) before the next cycle (D).”
mpt-course-english-d17q1.e: Suggest takes the gerund: suggested reconsidering.

mpt-course-english-d17q10.q: She managed ____ the file before the office closed.

mpt-course-english-d17q2.q: Which sentence means that he gave up the habit?
o: He stopped in order to smoke.
He has stopped to smoke daily.
He stopped to smoke outside the building.
He stopped smoking two years ago.
mpt-course-english-d17q2.e: stop + -ing means to end an activity; stop + to means to pause in order to do something.

mpt-course-english-d17q3.q: I regret ____ you that your application has been rejected.
mpt-course-english-d17q3.e: regret + to + verb introduces the bad news you are delivering now.

mpt-course-english-d17q4.q: Find the error: “The department denied (A) to have received (B) the representation (C) within the stipulated period (D).”
mpt-course-english-d17q4.e: Deny takes the gerund: denied having received.

mpt-course-english-d17q5.q: ____ the accounts carefully, the auditor identified three irregularities.
mpt-course-english-d17q5.e: The perfect participle marks the earlier of the two actions, and the auditor is the doer of both.

mpt-course-english-d17q7.q: ____ clear rules is easier than enforcing them.
mpt-course-english-d17q7.e: A gerund heads the subject and pairs naturally with the gerund after than.

mpt-course-english-d17q9.q: Which sentence uses the participle correctly?
o: Having written in haste, the note was unclear.
Writing in haste, the note contained three errors.
Written in haste, the note contained three errors.
Written in haste, the officer signed the note.
mpt-course-english-d17q9.e: The note was written in haste, so the past participle correctly describes the note.

mpt-course-english-d18q3.q: His performance in the interview was not so impressive ____ his written papers.
mpt-course-english-d18q3.e: Not so … as is the fixed pattern of negative equality.

mpt-course-english-d18q5.q: The sooner the file is cleared, ____.
mpt-course-english-d18q5.e: The parallel pattern is the sooner … the better.

mpt-course-english-d18q9.q: The Indus is longer than ____ river in South Asia.
mpt-course-english-d18q9.e: The Indus is a South Asian river, so it must be excluded from the group.

mpt-course-english-d19q10.q: Find the error: “As the rains failed (A), so the wheat output (B) fell by (C) nine per cent (D).”
mpt-course-english-d19q10.e: As already marks the cause; so must go.

mpt-course-english-d19q2.q: The project was abandoned ____ a shortage of funds.
mpt-course-english-d19q2.e: A noun phrase follows, so a prepositional connector is required.

o: She is responsible not only for revenue but also excise.
She is responsible not only for revenue but also for excise.
She is not only responsible for revenue but also excise.
She not only is responsible for revenue but also for excise.
mpt-course-english-d19q3.e: Each half of the pair is followed by the same structure: for + noun.

mpt-course-english-d19q8.q: The scheme was designed ____ small farmers could obtain credit without collateral.
mpt-course-english-d19q8.e: A clause with its own subject follows, so so that is required.

mpt-course-english-d19q9.q: Which sentence shows contrast between two simultaneous facts?
o: Punjab raised its education budget, therefore Sindh reduced its own.
Punjab raised its education budget, whereas Sindh reduced its own.
Punjab raised its education budget, moreover Sindh reduced its own.
Punjab raised its education budget because Sindh reduced its own.
mpt-course-english-d19q9.e: Whereas marks a direct contrast between two parallel facts.

mpt-course-english-d1q10.q: Find the error: “Decision (A) to postpone the examination (B) was announced (C) on Friday (D).”
mpt-course-english-d1q10.e: A singular countable noun cannot stand alone as a subject. Write “The decision”.

mpt-course-english-d1q2.q: A significant ____ of complaints was received by the ombudsman.
mpt-course-english-d1q2.e: Complaints are countable, so number is correct. Amount belongs with uncountable nouns.

o: She performed well in the interview.
She performed good in the interview.
She performed a good in the interview.
She performed goodly in the interview.
mpt-course-english-d1q3.e: Performed is an action verb, so it needs the adverb well, not the adjective good.

mpt-course-english-d1q5.q: The policy was ____ criticised by independent economists.
mpt-course-english-d1q5.e: The word describes the participle criticised, so an adverb is required.

mpt-course-english-d1q6.q: In which sentence is fund used as a verb?
o: Donors will fund the second phase.
mpt-course-english-d1q6.e: In option B, fund carries the action after the modal will, so it is a verb.

mpt-course-english-d1q8.e: Appear is a linking verb, so the adjective convincing follows it.

mpt-course-english-d1q9.q: The candidate worked ____ throughout the year but ____ took a day of leave.
mpt-course-english-d1q9.e: Hard means with effort; hardly means almost not. The sentence needs one of each, in that order.

mpt-course-english-d20q10.q: Which set of bullet points is parallel?
o: Improving enrolment; training teachers; reducing dropout
Improve enrolment; teacher training; to reduce dropout
Enrolment improvement; train teachers; reducing dropout
Improve enrolment; training teachers; dropout reduction
mpt-course-english-d20q10.e: All three begin with a gerund.

o: Drafting a summary is harder than a note.
To draft a summary is harder than drafting a note.
Drafting a summary is harder than drafting a note.
Drafting a summary is harder than to draft a note.

mpt-course-english-d20q7.q: Find the error: “Candidates must either submit (A) the original degree (B) or they should attach (C) an attested copy (D).”
mpt-course-english-d20q7.e: Either … or must join like with like: “or attach an attested copy”.

o: The section officer examined the file and the deputy secretary approved it.
The file was examined by the section officer and the deputy secretary approved it.
The section officer examined the file and it was approved by the deputy secretary.
The file was examined by the section officer and approved the deputy secretary.
mpt-course-english-d20q8.e: Both clauses stay active, so the sentence reads as one movement.

mpt-course-english-d20q9.q: Find the error: “He is responsible for planning (A), for budgeting (B) and to monitor (C) the annual programme (D).”
mpt-course-english-d20q9.e: The third item must be for monitoring.

mpt-course-english-d21q1.q: Find the error: “The commission performs: (A) four functions (B) — advising, inspecting, (C) reporting and recommending (D).”
mpt-course-english-d21q1.e: A colon cannot stand between a verb and its object. Delete it: “The commission performs four functions — advising, inspecting …”.

mpt-course-english-d21q3.q: Find the error: “The delegates came from Lahore, Punjab, (A) Quetta, Balochistan, (B) and Gilgit (C) last Tuesday (D).”
mpt-course-english-d21q3.e: Because the items contain internal commas, they must be separated by semicolons: “Lahore, Punjab; Quetta, Balochistan; and Gilgit”.

mpt-course-english-d21q5.q: Find the error: “The tribunal described the delay as, (A) “wholly unexplained” (B) and ordered (C) an inquiry (D).”
mpt-course-english-d21q5.e: A partial quotation after as takes no comma.

mpt-course-english-d21q7.q: Find the error: “The scheme failed; (A) although the funds (B) had been released (C) in time (D).”
mpt-course-english-d21q7.e: A semicolon cannot precede a dependent clause; a comma or nothing is correct here.

mpt-course-english-d21q9.q: Find the error: “Only one province (A) — Balochistan, (B) was excluded (C) from the scheme (D).”
mpt-course-english-d21q9.e: The insertion must close with a second dash, not a comma.

mpt-course-english-d22q2.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
mpt-course-english-d22q2.q: Find the redundancy: “The committee reviewed (A) the past history (B) of the dispute (C) before deciding (D).”

mpt-course-english-d22q3.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
o: The auditor carried out an examination of the accounts.
An examination of the accounts was carried out by the auditor.
The accounts were subject to examination by the auditor.
mpt-course-english-d22q3.e: One verb replaces a four-word noun phrase.

mpt-course-english-d22q4.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
mpt-course-english-d22q4.q: Find the redundancy: “Each and every candidate (A) must bring (B) an original (C) identity card (D).”
mpt-course-english-d22q4.e: Each and every says the same thing twice.

mpt-course-english-d22q6.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
mpt-course-english-d22q6.q: Replace “in the event that the appeal is dismissed”.
o: when there is an appeal dismissal event
at the time of the dismissal of the appeal
mpt-course-english-d22q6.e: If carries the whole meaning in one word.

mpt-course-english-d22q7.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
mpt-course-english-d22q7.q: Find the redundancy: “The file was returned back (A) to the section (B) on the following (C) Monday (D).”
mpt-course-english-d22q7.e: Return already contains the idea of back.

mpt-course-english-d22q8.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
mpt-course-english-d22q8.q: Which sentence is both concise and complete?
o: The policy, it is possible to say, has had an effect which is limited.
It may be said that the policy has, to some extent, had some effect.
The policy has had a limited effect.
mpt-course-english-d22q8.e: The qualification survives; the throat-clearing does not.

mpt-course-english-d22q9.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
mpt-course-english-d22q9.q: Find the wordy phrase: “The department will act (A) at this point in time (B) to reduce (C) the backlog (D).”
mpt-course-english-d22q9.e: At this point in time means now.

mpt-course-english-d23q1.q: Find the error: “The report shows (A) that the scheme’s effect (B) on rural incomes (C) was continual and unbroken (D).”
mpt-course-english-d23q1.e: Continual means repeated with breaks, so it contradicts unbroken. Use continuous.

mpt-course-english-d23q10.q: Which replaces “find out the reason for the delay” formally?
o: figure out why it was late
establish the cause of the delay
get to the bottom of the delay
mpt-course-english-d23q10.e: Establish and cause are the formal equivalents.

mpt-course-english-d23q2.q: Which version is best for an examination answer?
o: Honestly speaking, the reforms were a total failure.
The reforms, you can see, were useless.
The reforms failed to achieve their stated objectives.
I think the reforms didn’t work out.

mpt-course-english-d23q3.q: From the minister’s silence the press ____ that a decision had already been taken.
mpt-course-english-d23q3.e: The listener infers; the speaker implies.

mpt-course-english-d23q4.q: Find the error: “The committee comprises of (A) seven members (B), three of whom (C) are officials (D).”
mpt-course-english-d23q4.e: Comprise takes no of. Write “comprises seven members” or “is composed of seven members”.

mpt-course-english-d23q5.q: Which sentence hedges appropriately without becoming empty?
o: Enforcement has definitely and completely collapsed.
It may possibly perhaps be the case that enforcement has weakened.
The data suggest that enforcement has weakened.

mpt-course-english-d23q6.q: The measure was ____ rather than political: it saved money.
mpt-course-english-d23q6.e: Economical means thrifty; economic relates to the economy.

mpt-course-english-d23q9.q: Candidates should ____ précis writing daily; regular ____ is essential.
mpt-course-english-d23q9.e: In British usage practise is the verb and practice the noun.

o: The law was changed six months later. The tribunal reserved judgement.
Six months later the law changed. Judgement had been reserved.
The tribunal reserved judgement. The law was changed by the judgement six months later.
The tribunal reserved judgement. That judgement, delivered six months later, changed the law.
mpt-course-english-d24q1.e: The new element at the end of the first sentence becomes the given at the start of the second.

mpt-course-english-d24q2.q: Find the shift: “A candidate who prepares systematically (A) will find that you retain more (B) and that your revision (C) becomes faster (D).”
mpt-course-english-d24q2.e: The third-person subject shifts to the second person. Keep he, she, they or the candidate throughout.

mpt-course-english-d24q3.q: Which summary noun best continues: “Three districts refused to implement the order.”?
o: This refusal was never formally recorded.
mpt-course-english-d24q3.e: A precise summary noun both links and judges.

mpt-course-english-d24q4.q: Which paragraph opening is a true topic sentence?
o: There are many problems with enforcement.
Enforcement, not legislation, is the binding constraint.
In 2019, the smog emergency was declared.
mpt-course-english-d24q4.e: It states one arguable claim the paragraph can support.

mpt-course-english-d24q5.q: Find the break in cohesion: “The policy was announced in March (A). The provinces were not consulted by the ministry (B). Implementation began in June (C). The cost has not been disclosed (D).”
mpt-course-english-d24q5.e: The voice shifts to the passive with no reason, breaking the chain of subjects.

mpt-course-english-d24q6.q: Which sentence uses ellipsis correctly for concision?
o: The first proposal was costly; the second, less so.
The first proposal was costly; the second proposal was less costly than the first proposal.
The first proposal was costly, the second was costly less.
The first proposal costly; second less.
mpt-course-english-d24q6.e: The repeated words are understood and need not be written.

mpt-course-english-d24q7.q: Which is the weaker use of a connector?
o: The funds lapsed, so the work stopped.
Because the funds lapsed, the work stopped.
The funds lapsed. The work therefore stopped.
The funds lapsed. Moreover, the work stopped.
mpt-course-english-d24q7.e: Moreover claims addition where the real relationship is cause and effect.

mpt-course-english-d24q9.q: Find the vague reference: “The department ignored two reminders and missed the deadline (A). This (B) was reported to the secretary (C) in writing (D).”
mpt-course-english-d24q9.e: This could mean the reminders, the omission or the delay. Write “This failure” or name it.

mpt-course-english-d25q10.q: Find the error: “The government will analyze (A) the programme (B) and publish (C) its defence (D) of the policy.”
mpt-course-english-d25q10.e: The rest of the sentence uses British spelling, so analyse is required. Keep one system throughout.

mpt-course-english-d25q5.q: An ____ economist warned that a collapse was ____.
mpt-course-english-d25q5.e: Eminent means distinguished; imminent means about to happen.

mpt-course-english-d25q8.q: The two candidates differed on many points; the ____ was better prepared.
mpt-course-english-d25q8.e: Latter means the second of two; later refers to time.

mpt-course-english-d26q1.q: Find the error: “The number of applications (A) received this year (B) have exceeded (C) all previous records (D).”
mpt-course-english-d26q1.e: Pass 1: the head noun is number, which is singular — has exceeded.

mpt-course-english-d26q10.q: Two corrections are possible for “If I would have known, I would have informed you.” Which changes fewer words?
o: If I had known, I would have informed you.
Had I known, I would have informed you.
Knowing that, I would have informed you.
I would have informed you if I had been aware.
mpt-course-english-d26q10.e: Replacing would have with had changes two words and keeps the structure.

mpt-course-english-d26q2.q: Which is the minimum correction of “The quality of the answers were disappointing”?
o: The quality of the answers was disappointing.
The answers were disappointing in quality.
The answers disappointed in their quality.
mpt-course-english-d26q2.e: One verb form is at fault; nothing else moves.

mpt-course-english-d26q3.q: Find the error: “She has been working (A) in this department (B) since the last (C) five years (D).”
mpt-course-english-d26q3.e: A duration takes for, not since the last: “for the last five years”.

o: The committee have announced its decision.
The committee has announced their decision.
The committee has announced its decision.
The committee have announced their decision.
mpt-course-english-d26q4.e: Singular verb and singular pronoun, consistently.

mpt-course-english-d26q5.q: Find the error: “Neither the clerk (A) nor the officers (B) was aware (C) of the change (D).”
mpt-course-english-d26q5.e: Nor points the verb at the nearer subject, officers, so were is required.

mpt-course-english-d26q6.q: Which is the minimum correction of “He suggested to postpone the meeting”?
o: He proposed that the meeting be postponed.
He wanted to postpone the meeting.
He said the meeting should be postponed.
mpt-course-english-d26q6.e: Only the form after suggested is wrong; one word changes.

mpt-course-english-d26q7.q: Find the error: “The population of Karachi (A) is greater (B) than Lahore (C) by several million (D).”
mpt-course-english-d26q7.e: Compare like with like: “than that of Lahore”. Two words are inserted, and nothing else moves.

mpt-course-english-d26q9.q: Find the error: “Having reviewed the file (A), a decision (B) was taken (C) to close the case (D).”
mpt-course-english-d26q9.e: A decision did not review the file. The minimum repair names the doer: “the officer took a decision”.

mpt-course-english-d2q3.q: Improving literacy rates in rural districts ____ sustained funding.
mpt-course-english-d2q3.e: The whole -ing phrase is one singular subject.

mpt-course-english-d2q5.q: Which group of words is a complete sentence?
o: Although the budget was approved in March.
The budget approved in March by the assembly.
The budget was approved in March.
Approving the budget in March despite objections.
mpt-course-english-d2q5.e: Only option C has a subject and a finite verb and does not begin with a subordinator.

mpt-course-english-d2q6.q: What the tribunal decided in those two cases ____ still disputed.
mpt-course-english-d2q6.e: The subject is the whole what-clause, which counts as one singular idea.

mpt-course-english-d2q8.q: In “The board declared the contract void”, what is void?
mpt-course-english-d2q8.e: Void describes the object contract, so it is an object complement.

mpt-course-english-d2q9.q: Neither the chairman nor the members ____ willing to sign.
mpt-course-english-d2q9.e: With neither … nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, members.

mpt-course-english-d3q1.q: Find the error: “Even though (A) the department issued a clarification (B), but the confusion (C) continued for weeks (D).”
mpt-course-english-d3q1.e: Even though and but both mark contrast. Delete but.

mpt-course-english-d3q4.q: Find the error: “Because of (A) the applicant had submitted (B) the wrong form (C), the request was rejected (D).”
mpt-course-english-d3q4.e: A full clause follows, so because is required, not because of.

mpt-course-english-d3q5.q: Which group of words is a fragment?
o: The deadline, which passed last Monday, was final.
Since the deadline passed last Monday.
mpt-course-english-d3q5.e: Since makes the clause dependent, so it cannot stand alone.

mpt-course-english-d3q6.q: In “The report shows that enforcement has failed”, the that-clause works as
mpt-course-english-d3q6.e: It answers “shows what?”, so it is a noun clause working as the object.

mpt-course-english-d3q7.q: Find the error: “The villages, that were worst affected (A) by the floods (B), received relief (C) three weeks late (D).”
mpt-course-english-d3q7.e: Use which after a comma. That never introduces a non-defining clause.

mpt-course-english-d3q8.q: ____ the tribunal reserved its judgement, the parties waited outside.
mpt-course-english-d3q8.e: A clause follows, so a subordinator is needed; during and despite take nouns.

mpt-course-english-d5q2.q: The committee ____ its recommendations last Thursday.
mpt-course-english-d5q2.e: A collective noun acting as one body takes a singular verb.

mpt-course-english-d5q4.q: Attached to the application ____ three certificates.
mpt-course-english-d5q4.e: The subject, certificates, follows the verb and is plural.

mpt-course-english-d5q6.e: Most takes its number from evidence, which is uncountable and singular.

mpt-course-english-d5q9.q: Either the secretary or his deputies ____ to attend the briefing.
mpt-course-english-d5q9.e: The nearer subject, deputies, is plural.

mpt-course-english-d6q4.s: Capital letters, full stops and the everyday comma
mpt-course-english-d6q4.q: Find the error: “In 1947 (A) Pakistan (B) gained independence, (C) and adopted a new flag (D).”
mpt-course-english-d6q4.e: “adopted a new flag” has no subject of its own, so no comma is needed before and.

mpt-course-english-d7q10.s: Present and past: the four forms of each
mpt-course-english-d7q10.q: The file ____ four annexures and a covering note.
mpt-course-english-d7q10.e: Contain is stative and takes the simple form.

mpt-course-english-d7q4.s: Present and past: the four forms of each
mpt-course-english-d7q4.q: The novel ____ the collapse of a landed family in colonial Bengal.
mpt-course-english-d7q4.e: Discussion of a literary text uses the present simple.

mpt-course-english-d7q7.s: Present and past: the four forms of each
mpt-course-english-d7q7.q: While the delegates ____, the secretariat ____ the final draft.
mpt-course-english-d7q7.e: The longer background is continuous; the single completed act is past simple.

mpt-course-english-d8q10.q: Which sentence uses the present perfect correctly?
o: The commission has met three times yesterday.
The commission has met three times in 2019.
The commission has met three times last month.
The commission has met three times this month.
mpt-course-english-d8q10.e: This month is an unfinished period, so the present perfect fits.

mpt-course-english-d8q2.q: The roads are still wet because it ____ all night.
mpt-course-english-d8q2.e: The present perfect continuous stresses the activity that produced the present result.

mpt-course-english-d8q3.q: Which sentence correctly shows that the meeting ended before the minister arrived?
o: The meeting has ended before the minister arrived.
The meeting was ending before the minister arrived.
The meeting ended when the minister arrived.
The meeting had ended before the minister arrived.
mpt-course-english-d8q3.e: The past perfect marks the earlier of two past events.

mpt-course-english-d8q4.q: Prices ____ steadily since the imposition of the new duty.
mpt-course-english-d8q4.e: Since requires a perfect tense, and rise is the intransitive verb.

mpt-course-english-d8q6.q: How long ____ you ____ for the result?
mpt-course-english-d8q6.e: How long with an activity continuing to now takes the present perfect continuous.

mpt-course-english-d8q9.q: The file ____ on the table where the clerk had left it.
mpt-course-english-d8q9.e: Lie (to rest) has the past form lay; laid belongs to lay (to place something).

mpt-course-english-d9q1.s: Future forms and the sequence of tenses
mpt-course-english-d9q1.q: Find the error: “If the assembly (A) will pass the bill (B), the president (C) will sign it (D).”
mpt-course-english-d9q1.e: The if-clause takes the present simple: if the assembly passes the bill.

mpt-course-english-d9q10.s: Future forms and the sequence of tenses
mpt-course-english-d9q10.q: She promised that she ____ the documents the following day.
mpt-course-english-d9q10.e: Will backshifts to would after a past reporting verb.

mpt-course-english-d9q2.s: Future forms and the sequence of tenses
mpt-course-english-d9q2.q: The conference ____ on 12 April according to the published schedule.
mpt-course-english-d9q2.e: A published timetable takes the present simple.

mpt-course-english-d9q3.s: Future forms and the sequence of tenses
mpt-course-english-d9q3.q: Which sentence describes a fixed arrangement?
o: We will meet the registrar sometime.
We are meeting the registrar at eleven tomorrow.
mpt-course-english-d9q3.e: The present continuous with a stated time marks a fixed arrangement.

mpt-course-english-d9q5.s: Future forms and the sequence of tenses
mpt-course-english-d9q5.q: This time next week the candidates ____ the compulsory papers.
mpt-course-english-d9q5.e: An action in progress at a stated future point takes the future continuous.

mpt-course-english-d9q7.s: Future forms and the sequence of tenses
mpt-course-english-d9q7.q: The teacher explained that light ____ faster than sound.
mpt-course-english-d9q7.e: A scientific truth keeps the present tense after a past reporting verb.

mpt-course-english-d9q8.s: Future forms and the sequence of tenses
mpt-course-english-d9q8.q: Find the error: “By the time the inquiry concludes (A), the officer (B) will retire (C) from service (D).”
mpt-course-english-d9q8.e: By the time + a future point requires the future perfect: will have retired.

mpt-course-english-d9q9.s: Future forms and the sequence of tenses
mpt-course-english-d9q9.q: Which sentence shows an intention formed before speaking?
o: I would apply for the post.
I will apply for the post.
I am going to apply for the post.
mpt-course-english-d9q9.e: Going to signals a plan already decided.

mpt-current-expanded-057.q: What share of athletes at Milano Cortina 2026 were women, according to the official Games figures?

mpt-current-expanded-058.q: How many competition venues were listed for Milano Cortina 2026?
mpt-current-expanded-058.e: The official information listed 13 competition venues.

mpt-current-expanded-061.q: Which new skeleton event appeared at Milano Cortina 2026?
mpt-current-expanded-061.e: A mixed-team skeleton event was introduced.

mpt-current-expanded-062.q: Which freestyle-skiing event was newly added at Milano Cortina 2026?
mpt-current-expanded-062.e: Men’s and women’s dual moguls were added.

mpt-current-expanded-063.q: Where was the opening ceremony of Milano Cortina 2026 staged?
mpt-current-expanded-063.e: The opening ceremony took place at Milan’s San Siro Stadium.

mpt-current-expanded-064.q: Where was the closing ceremony of Milano Cortina 2026 staged?
mpt-current-expanded-064.e: The Arena di Verona served as the Verona Olympic Arena for the closing ceremony.

mpt-current-expanded-066.q: Khalilur Rahman, elected President of UNGA 81, represented which country?

mpt-current-expanded-070.q: From which regional group was the President of UNGA 81 due to be elected under rotation?
mpt-current-expanded-070.e: The established rotation allocated the election to the Asia-Pacific Group.

mpt-current-verified-006.q: Which Pakistani programme had its third review completed by the IMF Board in May 2026?
mpt-current-verified-006.e: The Board completed the third review of Pakistan’s Extended Fund Facility.

mpt-current-verified-007.q: About how much did the May 2026 IMF decision make immediately drawable for Pakistan under the EFF?
mpt-current-verified-007.e: The EFF decision permitted an immediate disbursement of about US$1.1 billion.

mpt-current-verified-009.q: During which dates does the UNFCCC schedule COP31 in November 2026?
mpt-current-verified-009.e: The UNFCCC schedules COP31 for 9–20 November 2026.

mpt-current-verified-011.q: Which country is working in partnership with Türkiye for the incoming COP31 presidency?
mpt-current-verified-011.e: The UNFCCC describes the Türkiye–Australia partnership arrangements for COP31.

mpt-current-verified-012.q: The WHO’s 2026 negotiations on a key annex to its Pandemic Agreement concerned which mechanism?
mpt-current-verified-012.e: WHO member states were negotiating the Pathogen Access and Benefit Sharing annex.

mpt-past-papers-352.q: If BAT is coded as 283, CAT is coded as 383 and ARE is coded as 801, then the code for BETTER is:

mpt-past-papers-370.q: P is the brother of Q and R. S is mother of R, and T is father of P. Which of the following statements is not exactly true?

mpt-past-papers-371.q: Arrange the given words in the order that they occur in dictionary: 1. Apparent 2. Apostate 3. Appoint 4. Apparel

mpt-past-papers-502.q: درج ذیل الفاظ میں سے کون سا لفظ مونث ہے؟

mpt-past-papers-506.q: "مشاہرہ" کا ہم معنی لفظ کون سا ہے؟

mpt-past-papers-509.q: دو یا دو سے زیادہ الفاظ کے مجموعے کو _____ کہا جاتا ہے۔

mpt-past-papers-510.q: Preposterous کا درست ترجمہ کیا ہے؟

mpt-past-papers-511.q: Move heaven and earth کا درست ترجمہ کیا ہے؟

mpt-past-papers-514.q: _____ وہ اسم ہے جو اعزاز کے طور پر حکومت، بادشاہ یا عوام الناس کی طرف سے ملتا ہے۔

mpt-past-papers-516.q: لفظ Economy کا درست اردو متبادل کیا ہے؟

mpt-past-papers-521.q: "Minutes of the Meeting" کا درست اردو متبادل کیا ہے؟

mpt-reviewed-past-ability-248.q: A jug contains 2 litres of a mixture of apple juice and orange juice in the ratio 3:5. We take out 400 ml of juice from the jug. How much more apple juice needs to be added so that the ratio becomes 7:5?
mpt-reviewed-past-ability-248.e: Initially there are 750 ml apple and 1,250 ml orange. After removing 400 ml uniformly, 600 ml apple and 1,000 ml orange remain. (600+x)/1,000=7/5 gives x=800 ml.

mpt-reviewed-past-ability-273.q: Find the number which does not fit in the series: 10, 25, 45, 54, 60, 75, 85
mpt-reviewed-past-ability-273.e: Every listed number except 54 is divisible by five; 54 is the outlier.

mpt-reviewed-past-ability-274.q: A new number is added to the series 3, 4, 4, 5, 6, 8 such that the average of the series does not change. What is the new number?
mpt-reviewed-past-ability-274.e: The six existing terms total 30 and average 5. Adding their mean leaves the average unchanged.

mpt-reviewed-past-ability-278.q: A watchmaker sold 40 percent of his watches and still has 420 watches left. How many did he have to begin with?
mpt-reviewed-past-ability-278.e: The 420 watches remaining represent 60% of the original stock; 420/0.60=700.

mpt-reviewed-past-ability-279.q: Six years ago, the ratio of the ages of Ali and Babar was 6:5. Four years from now, the ratio of their ages will be 11:10. What is Babar's age at present?
mpt-reviewed-past-ability-279.e: Six years ago the ages were 6x and 5x. Four years later they will be 6x+10 and 5x+10. Their ratio 11:10 gives x=2; Babar is now 5x+6=16.

mpt-reviewed-past-ability-286.q: Several number of cows on a farm consume the food in 150 days. If we reduce the number of cows by 10, then the food lasts for 160 days. How many cows were there on the farm in the beginning?
mpt-reviewed-past-ability-286.e: If N cows consume a fixed store in 150 days, then 150N=160(N−10). Solving gives N=160.

mpt-reviewed-past-ability-295.q: The first term in a sequence is 1 and the second term is 5. From the third term onwards, each term is the average (arithmetic mean) of all preceding terms. What is the 27th term in the sequence?
mpt-reviewed-past-ability-295.e: The third term is (1+5)/2=3. The mean of 1,5,3 remains 3, so every later term, including the 27th, is 3.

mpt-reviewed-past-ability-299.q: A water tank in the shape of a cuboid has length 1.5 metres and width 1.0 metre. How many litres of water are in the tank if the water is 60 centimetres deep?
mpt-reviewed-past-ability-299.e: The water volume is 1.5×1.0×0.60=0.9 m³. As 1 m³ is 1,000 litres, the tank holds 900 litres at that depth.

mpt-reviewed-past-ability-301.q: In a group of 200 people, 90 like tennis, while 108 like cricket and 46 people like both tennis and cricket. How many people like neither tennis nor cricket?
mpt-reviewed-past-ability-301.e: By inclusion and exclusion, 90+108−46=152 like at least one game; 200−152=48 like neither.

mpt-reviewed-past-ability-302.q: 450 visitors visit a museum on each Monday, while only 120 visit on each of the remaining six days of the week. How many visitors are there on a daily average basis in a month of 30 days beginning on a Monday?

mpt-reviewed-past-ability-307.q: The forest workers plant 200 trees in one month (30 days). When 20 workers were sent away, 200 trees were planted in 40 days by this second group. How many workers were there in the first group?

mpt-reviewed-past-ability-313.q: A student spends 15% of his scholarship grant on food and 45% on tuition. After spending 50% of the remaining grant on his hostel fee, he is left with Rs 8,000 only. How much is his scholarship grant?

mpt-reviewed-past-ability-317.q: At a football match, the price of child ticket is Rs. 240 less than the adult ticket. There are 18,500 adults and 2500 children attending the match. Total amount paid for tickets is Rs. 41,400,000. What is the price of an adult ticket?
mpt-reviewed-past-ability-317.e: If the adult ticket costs p, the child ticket costs p−240. Then 18,500p+2,500(p−240)=41,400,000, giving p=Rs 2,000.

mpt-reviewed-past-ability-321.q: The lights and brakes of 30 bicycles were tested. 27 bicycles passed the lights and 21 passed the brakes test. The lights and brakes both failed on one bicycle. How many bicycles passed both tests?
mpt-reviewed-past-ability-321.e: Of 30 bicycles, one failed both, so 29 passed at least one. Passed both = 27+21−29=19.

mpt-reviewed-past-ability-323.q: 16 men and 12 women can complete a work in 20 days. 18 women can complete the same work in 40 days. In how many days will 12 men and 27 women complete the same work?
